hints: Complete the square on $f(x) = x^2 - 6x + c$: $(x - 3)^2 - 9 + c$.
Identify the minimum value of $f(x)$, which is $c - 9$ at $x = 3$.
Set the minimum value strictly greater than $2$: $c - 9 > 2$, and solve for $c$.
walkthrough:
Complete the square for the quadratic function $f(x) = x^2 - 6x + c$:
$$f(x) = (x - 3)^2 - 3^2 + c = (x - 3)^2 + c - 9$$

Identify the minimum value of $f(x)$ for $x \in \mathbb{R}$:
$$\text{Since } (x - 3)^2 \ge 0 \text{ for all } x, \quad \min(f(x)) = c - 9 \quad (\text{at } x = 3)$$

Apply the condition that $f(x) > 2$ for all $x$:
$$c - 9 > 2 \implies c > 11$$

State the set of possible values of $c$:
$$c > 11 \quad \text{or} \quad (11, \infty)$$
